quests.hint: Stress 'talking' and 'test' to set up the contrast.
quests.explanation: 'The whole point of… was to…' explains a purpose, and 'not to' adds what it wasn't.
quests.textToSpeak: The whole point of the exercise was to get people talking, not to test how much grammar they knew.
quests.correctAnswer: The whole point of the exercise was to get people talking, not to test how much grammar they knew.

quests.explanation: 'It's easy to underestimate' is a natural way to introduce something people often overlook.
quests.textToSpeak: It's easy to underestimate how tiring it is to concentrate in a second language all day long.
quests.correctAnswer: It's easy to underestimate how tiring it is to concentrate in a second language all day long.

quests.explanation: 'If anything' says the result was the opposite of what was hoped, and 'stopped + -ing' describes quitting a habit.
quests.textToSpeak: If anything, the extra training made things worse, because people stopped trusting their own instincts.
quests.correctAnswer: If anything, the extra training made things worse, because people stopped trusting their own instincts.

quests.explanation: Thanking the customer for waiting, then promising an update, is standard support language.
quests.textToSpeak: I appreciate your patience while we look into this, and I'll update you as soon as I have any news.
quests.correctAnswer: I appreciate your patience while we look into this, and I'll update you as soon as I have any news.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Patience' /ˈpeɪʃns/. 'Appreciate' /əˈpriːʃieɪt/. 'Update' as a verb /ʌpˈdeɪt/. 'As soon as' links: az-soon-az.

quests.hint: Stress 'do' for a more sincere apology.
quests.explanation: 'Do apologize' uses emphatic 'do', and 'complimentary' here means free.
quests.textToSpeak: We do apologize for the inconvenience, and we'd like to offer you a complimentary upgrade on your next stay.
quests.correctAnswer: We do apologize for the inconvenience, and we'd like to offer you a complimentary upgrade on your next stay.

quests.hint: 'Let me see' is a thinking phrase.
quests.explanation: 'I should warn you' prepares the listener for information they may not like.
quests.textToSpeak: Let me see what I can do, although I should warn you that refunds usually take about ten working days.
quests.correctAnswer: Let me see what I can do, although I should warn you that refunds usually take about ten working days.

quests.explanation: Reception staff use this to explain delays, and 'running behind' means late.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm afraid the doctor's had an emergency, so all of this morning's appointments are running about forty minutes behind.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm afraid the doctor's had an emergency, so all of this morning's appointments are running about forty minutes behind.

quests.explanation: 'Swap… for…' is the pattern for exchanging one option for another.
quests.textToSpeak: Would it be possible to swap my Thursday slot for something later in the day, or perhaps another day altogether?
quests.correctAnswer: Would it be possible to swap my Thursday slot for something later in the day, or perhaps another day altogether?

quests.explanation: 'Something's come up' is the common excuse for a change of plans, and 'any time after' offers an alternative.
quests.textToSpeak: Something's come up at work, so I'll have to move our call, but I'm free any time after four.
quests.correctAnswer: Something's come up at work, so I'll have to move our call, but I'm free any time after four.

quests.explanation: 'It still stung' expresses hurt honestly, and 'coming from' explains why it hurt.
quests.textToSpeak: I know she didn't mean it that way, but it still stung, especially coming from someone I trust.
quests.correctAnswer: I know she didn't mean it that way, but it still stung, especially coming from someone I trust.

quests.hint: 'For what it's worth' softens an opinion.
quests.explanation: This phrase offers encouragement without pushing it, and 'would have' ends the sentence without repeating 'handled'.
quests.textToSpeak: For what it's worth, I think you handled that situation far better than most people would have.
quests.correctAnswer: For what it's worth, I think you handled that situation far better than most people would have.

quests.explanation: 'Would mean a lot' expresses emotion gently, and 'make up your mind' means decide.
quests.textToSpeak: It would mean a lot to me if you could at least hear me out before making up your mind.
quests.correctAnswer: It would mean a lot to me if you could at least hear me out before making up your mind.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Making up' links: may-king-up. 'Mind' /maɪnd/ ends in /nd/. 'At least' links: a-tleast.

quests.explanation: 'Had barely… when…' shows one event almost immediately interrupted by another.
quests.textToSpeak: We'd barely sat down on the platform when the announcement came that our train had been cancelled.
quests.correctAnswer: We'd barely sat down on the platform when the announcement came that our train had been cancelled.

quests.hint: 'Fit us in' means find space for us.
quests.explanation: 'Fit someone in' is a hospitality phrase, and 'at no extra cost' means for free.
quests.textToSpeak: Since the hotel couldn't fit us in for the second night, they arranged somewhere nearby at no extra cost.
quests.correctAnswer: Since the hotel couldn't fit us in for the second night, they arranged somewhere nearby at no extra cost.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Arranged' /əˈreɪndʒd/. 'Nearby' /ˌnɪəˈbaɪ/ is stressed on BY. 'Couldn't' has a silent 'l'. 'Fit us' links.

quests.explanation: 'End up + -ing' shows an unplanned habit, and 'handy' means easy to reach.
quests.textToSpeak: You're supposed to keep your boarding pass handy, but I always end up digging through my bag for it.
quests.correctAnswer: You're supposed to keep your boarding pass handy, but I always end up digging through my bag for it.

quests.hint: Stress 'fix' and 'faster' to show the irony.
quests.explanation: 'Was supposed to' states an expectation that failed, and 'actually' adds surprise.
quests.textToSpeak: The update was supposed to fix the battery problem, but it's actually made it drain even faster.
quests.correctAnswer: The update was supposed to fix the battery problem, but it's actually made it drain even faster.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Battery' /ˈbætəri/. 'Drain' /dreɪn/ starts with /dr/. 'Update' as a noun is /ˈʌpdeɪt/. 'Even' /ˈiːvn/.

quests.hint: 'Just in case' is a fixed chunk.
quests.explanation: 'Recommend + -ing' is the pattern, and 'just in case' gives the reason for caution.
quests.textToSpeak: I'd recommend backing up everything before you try to restore the settings, just in case something goes wrong.
quests.correctAnswer: I'd recommend backing up everything before you try to restore the settings, just in case something goes wrong.

quests.hint: 'Never bother' + -ing shows a habit of not doing something.
quests.explanation: 'Surprisingly' introduces a fact that goes against expectation.
quests.textToSpeak: Surprisingly, most people never bother changing their default privacy settings, so their data is more exposed than they realize.
quests.correctAnswer: Surprisingly, most people never bother changing their default privacy settings, so their data is more exposed than they realize.

quests.hint: Use rising tone on the first two items and falling tone on the last.
quests.explanation: 'To sum up' introduces a summary, and a list of three items is a natural way to close a meeting.
quests.textToSpeak: To sum up, we've agreed to launch in March, keep the budget as it is, and review monthly.
quests.correctAnswer: To sum up, we've agreed to launch in March, keep the budget as it is, and review monthly.

quests.explanation: 'The main takeaway' is a business phrase for the key conclusion, and 'than they do about' compares priorities.
quests.textToSpeak: The main takeaway from the survey is that customers care more about reliability than they do about price.
quests.correctAnswer: The main takeaway from the survey is that customers care more about reliability than they do about price.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Survey' as a noun is /ˈsɜːveɪ/. 'Reliability' /rɪˌlaɪəˈbɪləti/ is stressed on BIL. 'Customers' /ˈkʌstəməz/.

quests.explanation: 'In short' introduces a summary, and 'iron out' is a common workplace idiom.
quests.textToSpeak: In short, the trial went better than expected, although we still need to iron out a few minor issues.
quests.correctAnswer: In short, the trial went better than expected, although we still need to iron out a few minor issues.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Trial' /ˈtraɪəl/. 'Minor' /ˈmaɪnə/. 'Expected' /ɪkˈspektɪd/. 'Iron' /ˈaɪən/ is often two syllables with a silent 'r'.

quests.hint: 'Better off' means in a better situation.
quests.explanation: 'You're better off + -ing' is a common advice frame, and 'unless' adds the exception.
quests.textToSpeak: You're better off waiting until the prices come down, unless you really need it before the end of the year.
quests.correctAnswer: You're better off waiting until the prices come down, unless you really need it before the end of the year.

quests.explanation: This sentence gives a cause-and-effect explanation, with 'pile up' meaning accumulate.
quests.textToSpeak: The trouble with putting things off is that they tend to pile up, and then everything feels urgent at once.
quests.correctAnswer: The trouble with putting things off is that they tend to pile up, and then everything feels urgent at once.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Urgent' /ˈɜːdʒənt/ has /dʒ/. 'Putting things' links. 'Tend to' links. 'At once' links: a-twunts.

quests.explanation: 'Be afraid to ask' is a common phrase for encouraging newcomers.
quests.textToSpeak: It's worth remembering that nobody expects you to know everything on your first day, so don't be afraid to ask.
quests.correctAnswer: It's worth remembering that nobody expects you to know everything on your first day, so don't be afraid to ask.

quests.explanation: 'By the time I noticed' places a discovery after the event, which is typical of a short story.
quests.textToSpeak: My phone slipped out of my pocket on the bus, and by the time I noticed, it was gone.
quests.correctAnswer: My phone slipped out of my pocket on the bus, and by the time I noticed, it was gone.

quests.hint: 'We'd' appears twice, with two different meanings.
quests.explanation: The past perfect continuous shows a long action before a discovery, and 'by then' marks the result.
quests.textToSpeak: We'd been driving for hours when we realized we'd taken the wrong exit, and by then it was completely dark.
quests.correctAnswer: We'd been driving for hours when we realized we'd taken the wrong exit, and by then it was completely dark.

quests.explanation: 'Started as… but turned into…' is a classic story arc, and 'that now employs' adds the result.
quests.textToSpeak: The whole thing started as a joke, but somehow it turned into a business that now employs twelve people.
quests.correctAnswer: The whole thing started as a joke, but somehow it turned into a business that now employs twelve people.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Employs' /ɪmˈplɔɪz/ is stressed on PLOY. 'Twelve' /twelv/. 'Somehow' /ˈsʌmhaʊ/. 'Business' /ˈbɪznɪs/ has a /z/ and two syllables.

quests.hint: 'Now that' gives a reason based on a new situation.
quests.explanation: 'Now that' explains how a change in circumstances leads to a realization, and 'worn off' means faded.
quests.textToSpeak: Now that the initial excitement has worn off, it's clear the project will need far more effort than anyone predicted.
quests.correctAnswer: Now that the initial excitement has worn off, it's clear the project will need far more effort than anyone predicted.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Initial' /ɪˈnɪʃl/ is stressed on NISH. 'Excitement' /ɪkˈsaɪtmənt/. 'Predicted' /prɪˈdɪktɪd/. 'Worn off' links.

quests.hint: Stress 'Friday' and 'two presentations' to show the load.
quests.explanation: 'Between X and Y' lists two things that explain why you're busy, and 'swamped' means overloaded.
quests.textToSpeak: I'd love to help, but between the deadline on Friday and the two presentations next week, I'm completely swamped.
quests.correctAnswer: I'd love to help, but between the deadline on Friday and the two presentations next week, I'm completely swamped.

quests.explanation: 'Make it' means attend, and 'engaging' describes a speaker who holds attention.
quests.textToSpeak: It's a shame you couldn't make it, because the speaker was really engaging and the questions afterwards were excellent.
quests.correctAnswer: It's a shame you couldn't make it, because the speaker was really engaging and the questions afterwards were excellent.
